thread:
anya-support: FYI ticket #AC-89321 — outbound wire pay_20260315_7788 ($142,300.00) was returned by the beneficiary bank. Bank reason: 'Invalid beneficiary account' / code: ACCT_FORMAT. Customer says they sent IBAN DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00

anya-support: Raw API request body from our logs (redacted):
```json
{
  "payment_id": "pay_20260315_7788",
  "amount": 14230000,
  "currency": "EUR",
  "beneficiary": {
    "name": "Acme Bio Ltd",
    "iban": "DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00 -EUR",
    "swift": "ERSTDEFF"
  }
}
```

payments-bot: Automated preflight: iban_normalized: "DE89370400440532013000-EUR" -> checksum_valid: false :warning:

mike-payments: :eyes: looks like the customer appended a suffix (-EUR) into the iban field. We strip non-alphanum but apparently the suffix remains attached after our normalization. Can you confirm raw payload exactly as received?

anya-support: Pasted above is exactly what we logged. Our pre-send sanitize currently does `replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g, \"\")` on the IBAN but it runs in the validation path, not the final send transform. So hyphen+letters stayed in the stored normalized string in some edge flows.

devon-eng: I can reproduce locally. If suffix stays, checksum fails and correspondent returns. Quick mitigation: run strict normalize then run IBAN checksum before queuing. I'll push a hotfix to the payments worker (canary) and add a metric for normalization failures.

sarah-finance: Customer wants reissue vs refund. We need bank MT103 trace to determine if funds are recoverable. I can hold for trace but if bank says loss, we will refund and ask customer to reinitiate with corrected IBAN.

mike-payments: Next steps: 1) Request MT103 from receiving bank via correspondent (we'll initiate trace). 2) Deploy normalization + checksum patch to payments-canary. 3) If trace shows returned funds, process refund; else reissue with corrected IBAN after customer confirmation.

devon-eng: Patch notes (brief):
```js
// normalize IBAN before checksum
const raw = beneficiary.iban || '';
const normalized = raw.replace(/[^A-Z0-9]/gi, '').toUpperCase();
if (!ibanValidate(normalized)) throw new Error('Invalid IBAN after normalization');
beneficiary.iban_normalized = normalized;
```
Deploy target: payments-canary -> canary-2026-03-15-3

anya-support: Shared update with customer and asked them to request MT103 from their bank. They also sent back the beneficiary bank's text: 'Intermediary refused: branch suffix "002" unknown' — might be a branch code appended after IBAN in their system.

mike-payments: If branch suffix is causing mismatch we may need to map branch code into the SWIFT/branch field or ask customer to put branch into separate field. I'll file a product ticket to add optional beneficiary.branch_code and a validation hint.

devon-eng: I'll add extra logging fields: raw_iban, normalized_iban, sanitize_errors for easier debugging next time. Will also add a small alert when normalization changes the string significantly (len diff > 3).

anya-support: Thanks team — updating support ticket. Will follow up once we get MT103 or the canary patch is live. :thumbsup:
